capabilities.title: Search the granted catalog
capabilities.description: Search catalog text and optionally restrict results by catalog type. Results are filtered by the authenticated user's library grants.
limitations: The route has no explicit argument for genre, release year, runtime, watched state, or other structured search constraints.
The API contract does not enumerate accepted values for the optional type argument.
This registry maps intent to existing service operations; it does not define a Lumi execution gateway.

capabilities.title: Read a Home catalog section
capabilities.description: Read Home rows such as continue watching, next up, recommendations, or a selected library row from the authenticated account's grant-filtered catalog.
limitations: The generated OpenAPI contract now includes recommendations as a Home section; Lumi workflow behavior and the capability mapping still require review.
The library section requires a libraryId and remains subject to account grants.
continueWatching is an authoritative continuation row, not proof of what is currently playing.

capabilities.title: Read a catalog item or its details
capabilities.description: Read grant-filtered catalog item data or detail sections for a known stable entity identifier.
limitations: An entity identifier must come from trusted catalog results or an explicitly versioned context fixture; the model must not invent identifiers.
A title in user text must be resolved through a grant-filtered catalog operation before an entity-specific read.

capabilities.title: Start playback for a resolved media target
capabilities.description: A proposed high-level assistant capability that resolves a user-provided target, requests a playable source, and asks the active ZenStream client to start it.
limitations: There is no Lumi-specific gateway that resolves target_text, handles ambiguous results, negotiates access, and starts the active client player.
target_text must never be inserted directly into an entity_id path; resolve it against grant-filtered trusted catalog results and clarify when the target is ambiguous.
A model action proposal does not authorize playback. The ZenStream server and active player remain responsible for validating access, current state, and user intent.
